title: Longest Arithmetic Sequence After Changing At Most One Element
summary: Given an integer array, determine the longest arithmetic subarray you can form by changing at most one element.
statement: Given an integer array, determine the longest arithmetic subarray you can form by changing at most one element. An arithmetic subarray has a constant difference between consecutive elements.
constraints: nums is a nonempty integer array.
Choose a contiguous subarray and change at most one of its elements to any integer.
Return the greatest possible length having one constant adjacent difference.
hints: Precompute unchanged arithmetic-run lengths ending and starting at every position.
A changed element can extend one side by one, or bridge both sides when its neighbors differ by an even amount.
For a bridge, use half the neighbor gap and join matching runs on each side.
Every optimal subarray places its optional change at an endpoint or interior bridge; the precomputed states evaluate all such locations exactly.
editorial: Every optimal subarray places its optional change at an endpoint or interior bridge; the precomputed states evaluate all such locations exactly.

tests.explanation: Changing ten to three makes the whole array 9,7,5,3,1 with difference -2.
Changing four to three makes all three elements arithmetic.
